name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+30 partisan lean makes it overwhelmingly Democratic
Raskin holds a roughly 400-to-1 fundraising advantage over Riley
High-profile incumbent with no history of competitive general elections
Prediction markets price the Democratic win probability near 97%
model.rationale: The district's D+30 lean, Raskin's roughly $9.3 million war chest against Riley's $22,000, and markets pricing the race near 97 percent Democratic leave virtually no path for the challenger; the only real uncertainty is the size of the margin, not the winner.
model.watch: A last-minute influx of outside spending for Riley or an unexpected scandal involving Raskin would be the only plausible sources of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jamie Raskin seeks another term in a Montgomery County-based district that ranks among the most Democratic in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 30 points. He enters the general election with an enormous financial edge, having raised more than $9 million and holding about $7.9 million on hand, while Republican Cheryl Riley has raised about $22,000. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign activity.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets price Raskin's chances at about 97 percent. The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, a well-known incumbent, and a minimally funded challenger makes an upset highly unlikely, though the absence of polling leaves the exact margin uncertain.
